title: Ex 2.6 #4 · ∼(P ∨ Q) = (∼P) ∧ (∼Q)
prompt: Use a truth table to show that $\sim (P \vee Q)$ and $(\sim P) \wedge (\sim Q)$ are logically equivalent: they have the same truth value in every row.
answer_format: No final answer box. Give the truth-table column of each statement as a column step (statement : T F T T, rows (P, Q) in the order TT, TF, FT, FF), or rewrite one statement into the other with expr steps, each equivalent to the one before.
hints: Find the column of P ∨ Q, then negate it.
For the right side, make columns for ∼P and ∼Q, then and them.
solution: $P \vee Q$ is T T T F, so $\sim (P \vee Q)$ is F F F T.
$\sim P$ is F F T T and $\sim Q$ is F T F T, so $(\sim P) \wedge (\sim Q)$ is F F F T.
The columns agree in every row, so the statements are logically equivalent. This is one of DeMorgan's laws.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
